title: Translation and constant Jacobian minors of a strictly standard presentation
statement: Let $R$, $\Lambda$ and $A$ be commutative rings, with $R$-algebra structures on $\Lambda$ and $A$, and suppose $A$ is finitely presented over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Let $\pi\in R$ and $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$ be an $R$-algebra map. Suppose the image of $\pi$ is strictly standard in $A$ [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element]. Write $q_A$, $q_R$, and $q_\Lambda$ for quotient maps modulo the ideals generated by the respective images of $\pi^4$. Assume an $R$-algebra map $\rho:A/(\pi^4)\to R/(\pi^4)$ exists such that, for all $a\in A$ and $r\in R$, $\rho(q_A(a))=q_R(r)$ implies $q_\Lambda(\alpha(a))=q_\Lambda(r)$. Then there exist natural numbers $n,m,c$, an $R$-algebra presentation $P$ with $n$ generators and $m$ relations [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], $c\le\min(n,m)$, scalars $a_j,t\in R$ and $\lambda_i\in\Lambda$ such that: $\alpha(P.val_i)=\pi^4\lambda_i$; the constant coefficient of $P.relation_j$ is $\pi^4a_j$; $(1-\pi^3t)\pi$ belongs to the ideal generated by the maximal row minors of the $n\times c$ matrix with entry in row $i$, column $j$ equal to the constant coefficient of $\partial_i P.relation_j$ [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative]; and for every $j\ge c$, $P.\sigma(\pi)P.relation_j$ belongs to $(P.relation_k\mid k<c)+(P.relation_k\mid k<m)^2$. Here $P.\sigma$ is the presentation's polynomial lift, and the polynomial ring is as in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring].

source.place: Stacks Project, Tag 07CR (lemma-desingularize), proof: choice of presentation through the identity for u pi, before use of Tag 07DQ

proof.text: Choose a presentation with c initial relations and Jacobian minors expressing the image of pi, together with the ideal-square condition for every remaining relation, by strict standardness. Choose lifts b_i in R of rho(P.val_i mod pi^4).

Let tau be the polynomial R-algebra automorphism sending x_i to x_i+b_i; its inverse sends x_i to x_i-b_i, since both composites fix constants and variables. Transport the relations by tau and the generator values to P.val_i-b_i. Transport the chosen polynomial lift P.sigma by tau as well. The universal property of the polynomial ring identifies the new evaluation composed with tau with the original evaluation, so its relation ideal is the kernel and the transported lift is still a right inverse.

Polynomial induction gives partial_i(tau(f))=tau(partial_i(f)): on constants and variables this is immediate, on sums it is additive, and on multiplication by a variable the two sides satisfy the same translated Leibniz rule. Determinants commute with tau by their finite sum formula. Thus the evaluated Jacobian minor identity is unchanged. Applying tau to the original ideal-square containment transports it to the new presentation; multiplication of ideals commutes with the automorphism.

The section on the new generators is zero. The composite R[x] to A to A/(pi^4) to R/(pi^4) and constant evaluation followed by R to R/(pi^4) agree on constants and variables, hence agree everywhere. Apply this identity to each relation to get constantCoeff(f_j)=pi^4 a_j. By compatibility with alpha, each alpha(P.val_i) has zero image in Lambda/(pi^4), so equals pi^4 lambda_i. These assertions use only the kernels of the principal-ideal quotient maps; no cancellation is involved.

Apply the section to the strictly standard minor identity, and choose scalar lifts d_I of the images of its finitely many coefficients. Constant evaluation commutes with the determinant by its finite sum formula. Thus pi minus sum_I d_I det(constantCoeff(partial_i f_j)) is in (pi^4), say pi^4 t. Rearranging gives (1-pi^3 t)pi=sum_I d_I det(constantCoeff(partial_i f_j)). Transposing each c by c minor leaves its determinant unchanged, so this is a linear combination of the maximal row minors in the statement, and in their ideal span.
